deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a continuous German prose text on Greek history, apparently lecture or reading notes. It runs on from p. 97, which covers the Spartan war in Asia Minor under Thimbron, Dercyllidas and Agesilaus and the battle of Haliartus, where Lysander fell. This page summarizes the following events:
(1) The battle of Coronea, where Agesilaus wins.
(2) The Spartan loss of naval supremacy: a Persian and Athenian fleet under Conon defeats Sparta at Cnidus.
(3) Conon returns to Athens and persuades the Athenians to rebuild their walls and fortify the city.
(4) The war drags on without major battles until the Peace of Antalcidas in 387. Persia dictates the terms, the Asiatic Greek colonies revert to Persia, and Sparta is charged with upholding the peace.
(5) Sparta becomes overbearing and in the following year undertakes expeditions against smaller cities. The marginal note gives examples: 'z.B. Mantinea und Phlius'.
The next page continues with Olynthus, the Spartan seizure of the Theban Cadmea by Phoebidas, and Epaminondas and Pelopidas. There are no formulas, computations or mathematical problems to reconstruct. The hand and content suggest school or university notes on ancient history; they were possibly not written by Gauss himself, and their placement in the bundle 'HB.Lagrange1816' is incidental.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.
Historical check: the dates broadly agree with standard chronology. Coronea and Cnidus are both 394 BC, and the Peace of Antalcidas (King's Peace) is 387/386 BC.

Minor historical simplification: the Cnidus victory was won by a Persian fleet under Pharnabazus and Conon. The Spartan action against Mantinea came in 385 and against Phlius in 384–379, so 'im folgenden Jahre' is approximate.

results.what: Narrative summary of the Corinthian War (Coronea, Cnidus, Conon's rebuilding of the Athenian walls) and the Peace of Antalcidas, followed by Spartan aggression against Mantinea and Phlius
results.modern_name: Corinthian War / King's Peace (387/386 BC); not mathematics

deep.surprise_reason: The page is ordinary historical lecture or reading notes on 4th-century BC Greek history with no mathematical content. Nothing here would surprise a historian of mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Lines 3-5: the image reads roughly 'zur See. / Die Flotte und persischen[?] und Atheniensischen / Schiffe hatten sich unter Conons Anführung gegen / sie verbündet, und diese ... schlug die Spartaner bei / Cnidus'. 'der Perser[?]' is uncertain; it may be 'und persischen'.
'Schutzherrschaft[?] des Friedens' more likely reads 'die Erhaltung des Friedens aufgetragen'. This fits Sparta's role as guarantor of the King's Peace.
'diktiren' is written 'dictiren', followed by a semicolon or stroke before 'Für'.
Marginal note: 'z.B. Mantinea und Phlius' is historically consistent; 'Phlius' is very probably correct.
The page number '98' in the top-left corner is in a different (archival) hand.
